stem: Mang Ramon used 3/4 of a sack of rice in the first week and 1/6 of a sack in the second week. What fraction of a sack did he use in all?
hints: "In all" means add. Before adding fractions, the bottom numbers must be the same.
Find a number that both 4 and 6 go into. 12 works: 4 × 3 = 12 and 6 × 2 = 12.
Change 3/4 to twelfths (multiply the top and the bottom by 3) and 1/6 to twelfths (multiply the top and the bottom by 2). Then add the tops and keep 12 on the bottom.

solution.methodName: Add or subtract fractions: make the bottoms the same first

steps.action: Find a common bottom. The smallest number that both 4 and 6 go into is 12.
steps.why: This is the least common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6. Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12. Count by 6s: 6, 12.
Multiply the top by the same number as the bottom, so the value does not change.

steps.action: Add the tops: 9 + 2 = 11. Keep the bottom: 12.
steps.why: The bottom only names the size of the pieces (twelfths). You add how many pieces you have, not their size.

steps.action: He used 11/12 of a sack in all.

trapNotes.4/10: This adds the tops (3 + 1) and the bottoms (4 + 6). Never add the bottoms; make them the same first.
trapNotes.7/12: This is 9/12 − 2/12. "In all" means add, not subtract.
trapNotes.4/12: This changes the bottoms to 12 but not the tops. 3/4 becomes 9/12 (not 3/12), and 1/6 becomes 2/12 (not 1/12).
